title: A triangle-free 40-vertex graph with independence number at most nine
statement: Does a finite simple undirected graph G on exactly 40 vertices exist with no triangle and no independent set of ten vertices? A positive witness proves R(3,10)=41; a complete impossibility proof proves R(3,10)=40, using the established interval 40 <= R(3,10) <= 41.
source_locator: DS1 revision 18, Table Ia and Section 2.1(d); Angeltveit, Theorem 1.1 and Section 7.
status_basis: The 2024 theorem and the survey dated 2026-04-24 leave exactly two values. A scoped search for a later resolution found none in authoritative sources as of 2026-10-14.

epistemic_layers.formal_validity: Only a checked finite witness or a proof covering the declared space establishes the mathematical claim.
epistemic_layers.empirical_support: No physical model, empirical data or experiment is needed.

difficulty.basis: The unrestricted target is a research frontier; a bounded trial has no assured outcome.

correctness.basis: No project candidate solution has been submitted or independently reviewed.

novelty.basis: Future results must be checked against live sources and existing computational records.

significance.basis: A positive witness resolves R(3,10), using the established upper bound.

plain_summary: One 40-vertex graph could decide which of two remaining values is R(3,10). Checking such a graph is easier than proving that every graph fails.
assumptions: The graph is simple, undirected and has exactly 40 vertices.
An independent set contains no graph edge; it is a clique in the complement.
No degree pattern, automorphism or source seed is assumed in the unrestricted statement.
scope: The remaining existence question for R(3,10). The proposed first milestone is a curator-selected neighborhood search, without a claim that those neighborhoods are themselves unsolved.
target: Construct a triangle-free 40-vertex graph with independence number at most nine. Proposed milestone: select at most 20 attributed 39-vertex source graphs, add one vertex with free adjacency, and permit at most four edge toggles among the original vertices.
success_criteria: Supply a complete graph serialization passing independent triangle and independent-ten-set checks.
Identify the seeds before searching; count edge changes on unordered pairs among the original 39 vertices only.
Cap the proposed trial at 8 CPU-hours and 16 GiB RAM. Retain witnesses, checked certificates and unresolved cases; these caps are planning choices, not measured performance.
UNSAT within selected seed neighborhoods is only a restricted result. Universal nonexistence requires an exhaustive decomposition covering all 40-vertex graphs.
known_results: Angeltveit's theorem, retained by the 2026 survey, leaves R(3,10) in {40,41}.
The survey describes a very large partial collection at order 39; a small selected seed set is not exhaustive.
Survey Section 2.1(i) excludes a lower-bound improvement from a circulant graph at this order.
significance: A positive witness determines an exact Ramsey number. A failed neighborhood search has narrower value and needs a novelty check before being called progress.

requirements.data: Attributed 39-vertex graph files from the author collection or paper records; validate and identify every selected seed.
requirements.compute: Proposed cap: 8 CPU-hours and 16 GiB RAM, at most 20 seeds. There are 780 possible edges. Triangle checking is small; excluding independent ten-sets needs exact branch-and-bound or a checked SAT certificate. No runtime guarantee is made.
requirements.theoretical_assumptions: Finite graph theory and the cited 40-to-41 interval. Every seed or edit restriction belongs only to the proposed trial.

ai_assessment.rationale: There is a decisive compact witness, but existing extensive searches make an arbitrary small neighborhood uncertain. Validate the checker and justify seed selection first.

clarity.reason: Fixed order and two forbidden substructures specify the task.

decomposability.reason: Seed validation, encoding, search and certification separate.

methods.reason: The primary paper and survey describe gluing, enumeration and constructions.

search_or_symbolic.reason: Adjacency variables admit exact finite constraints.

checkability.reason: The graph is small, but ruling out independent ten-sets requires exact computation.

expertise.reason: Useful restrictions require Ramsey and exhaustive-search expertise.

significance.reason: A witness settles the remaining two-valued exact-number question.

verification_difficulty.reason: Positive verification is bounded; global nonexistence is much harder.

ai_assessment.uncertainty: No model or proposed neighborhood has been tested. Published computations support the relevance of search, not the likelihood of success under this cap.
ai_assessment.model_scope: No named model evaluated; assumes tool-using AI with graph algorithms, exact SAT formulations and certificate handling.

methods: Seed extension with a declared edge-edit budget
Exact clique search in the complement
obstacles: Selected seeds cover only a small part of the known population.
An independent-set routine that stops early cannot certify the bound.
Unsound symmetry breaking can remove valid graphs.
Unverified historical web claims are not evidence of an exact value.

steps: Parse the witness independently and check order, symmetry and zero diagonal.
Use exact complement clique search or a separately checked UNSAT certificate to exclude a ten-clique.
Check the graph directly, not just the searcher's clauses.
Report restricted negative results with their seed list and edit radius.
validation.human_review_difficulty: Moderate for a graph with independent code and certificates; very high for universal nonexistence.
validation.statement_alignment: A 40-vertex witness plus the established upper bound gives 41. A failed restricted search gives no exact Ramsey value.

known_attempts: Angeltveit's Section 7 contains a partial order-39 census; Exoo's portal links a lower-bound graph. Neither is evidence about an AI system's measured ability.
unresolved_checks: Identify and validate seed files before a trial.
Check whether selected neighborhoods have already been exhausted.
Refresh the survey and primary result before an exact-value claim.

status_search.result: The primary result and April 2026 survey leave two values; the scoped October resolution check found no authoritative update.
status_search.limitations: Unpublished searches and every subsequent preprint have not been audited. Seed-neighborhood novelty is unverified.
